tier_reason: The gh-pages SVG chart (text read directly) shows the exact geomeans claimed: interpretation ulua 40.3 ms, Lua 5.4 40.4 ms, mlua/luau (Luau C++) 52.5 ms, LuaJIT 36.5 ms; JIT ulua 23 ms, mlua/luau 30.1 ms, LuaJIT 8.4 ms. The harness is public (bench.sh, benchmarks/runner/src/{main,engine,measure}.rs) and the runner's release profile is stated (opt-level 3, LTO, codegen-units 1), but no rustc or C/C++ compiler version is given, and the README names Apple Silicon while the chart footer names Neoverse-N2, so it is first-party with partial methodology and stays at C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: ulua and harness: Rust release profile in benchmarks/runner/Cargo.toml (opt-level 3, lto = true, codegen-units 1), mimalloc global allocator, -C target-feature=+aes on aarch64 from .cargo/config.toml. Luau C++, LuaJIT 2.1 and Lua 5.4 come from mlua 0.12 'vendored' features, built by the cc crate under the same Cargo profile. rustc and C/C++ compiler versions are not stated, and the repo has no rust-toolchain file.
corrections.caveats: The numbers are only in a chart image (benchmarks/benchmark-en.svg on gh-pages, deployed 2026-10-06); the README text claims only that ulua 'matches official C++ Luau throughput' in interpretation. The README says the medians were taken 'on Apple Silicon (arm64)', but the chart footer says Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 on Neoverse-N2 (4 cores). The harness times Lua::new() plus source compile plus run for every engine (symmetric), takes the minimum of 5 runs after 1 warm-up, and cross-checks return-value fingerprints. The chart has 8 cases, but benchmarks/cases now holds 16 and bench.sh mentions 24. Luau C++ comes through the mlua 0.12 binding (vendored luau, cc-built) and shows slower than PUC Lua 5.4, which suggests binding or build overhead in the baseline. bench.sh says the intended comparison basis is 'only the LuaJIT family', and the 2026-10-06 commits removed and then restored the engine-luau (mlua/luau) column. Not faster than Lua 5.4 in interpretation (tie); 2.7x slower than LuaJIT with JIT on. ulua is a refactor of pjankiewicz/luaur, a Rust translation of luau-lang/luau, which is already listed. The MIT licence is declared only in Cargo.toml and on crates.io (ulua 0.1.6); there is no LICENSE file in the repo.

notes: Confirmed at C: the claimed numbers match the chart exactly and the ratios are correctly marked derived. Shortcomings: README and chart disagree on the host (Apple Silicon vs Neoverse-N2), compiler versions are missing, the Luau baseline runs through the mlua binding and comes out slower than Lua 5.4, the benchmark config was edited the day the chart was deployed, ulua only ties Lua 5.4 in interpretation, and there is no LICENSE file (MIT only in Cargo metadata). Baseline luau-lang/luau is already a verified entry. ulua is a derived Rust port of Luau, not a duplicate.

tier_reason: Upgraded C to A for the QuickJS-NG headline. bench/comparison/README.md gives the public harness (bench/comparison/run_native.py over the bench/real 13-case corpus) and Zipp's compiler and flags (Rust/Cargo 1.92.0, release profile: opt-level 3, fat LTO, one codegen unit, no RUSTFLAGS, no PGO). The baseline is the official QuickJS-NG v0.16.2 qjs-windows-x86_64.exe, pinned by SHA-256 and built by upstream CI under MSYS2 UCRT64 in CMake Release mode (exact GCC revision unstamped), and the host is named as AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D on Windows 11. The Node/Bun/Deno numbers alone would be C: they were measured at 8229b3fc, before B280 fixed call ordering that was 'observably wrong for a getter or proxy trap', and the later capture is slower.

corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, Windows 11 (bench/comparison/README.md); the raw canonical JSON reports platform 'Windows-10-10.0.26200-SP0', processor 'AMD64 Family 26 Model 68 Stepping 0, AuthenticAMD'
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zipp: Rust/Cargo 1.92.0, repository release profile (opt-level 3, fat LTO, codegen-units 1, aborting panics), default features, no extra RUSTFLAGS and no PGO for the QuickJS-NG and Boa runs; the Node/Bun/Deno capture used a Windows PGO build via tools/pgo.sh. QuickJS-NG: official v0.16.2 release binary qjs-windows-x86_64.exe (SHA-256 7b27412de844403545bd151fbe49191b4d5b91a9e15b5db7c863fea54639a82b), built by upstream CI under MSYS2 UCRT64 in CMake Release mode with static mimalloc; exact compiler package revision not stamped.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Interpreter (ZIPP_NOJIT=1) vs QuickJS-NG v0.16.2 on real13: v0.0.5 startup-adjusted geomean 0.6413x of QuickJS-NG's time (cold 0.6439x; 12 of 13 point wins; about 1.56x faster, derived from page data); v0.0.6 at e3acee352074 cold 0.6090x and startup-adjusted 0.6058x (13 of 13 wins; about 1.64x faster, derived from page data). micro5 vs QuickJS-NG: 0.8556x startup-adjusted (5 of 5). With JITs on, vs Node v24.12.0 / Bun 1.3.14 / Deno 2.6.10 (canonical PGO capture at 8229b3fc): 0.728x / 0.594x / 0.460x across all 30 rows; 0.614x / 0.531x / 0.521x on the 13 normal rows; 0.878x / 0.752x / 0.765x on the retained ten without the three architecture diagnostics; hostile 17 0.829x Node. Median launch 7.4 ms vs Node 30.4 ms, Bun 43.3 ms, Deno 82.6 ms.
corrections.caveats: First-party, self-labelled diagnostic captures (diagnostic_only:true) with only six repetitions for the QuickJS-NG runs. The QuickJS-NG raw result JSONs sit in gitignored target/comparison/results by policy; only summaries and hashes are committed. The QuickJS-NG ratios are for v0.0.5 and v0.0.6 and were not rerun on current main (0.0.21). The Node/Bun/Deno canonical capture at 8229b3fc predates B280 (v0.0.15), which fixed method-call ordering that was 'observably wrong for a getter or proxy trap'. The later 14770703 capture is slower (headline ten 1.0025x Node, all 13 0.677x), and no headline is claimed for it. The 13-normal geomean (0.614x Node) leans on three architecture diagnostics (property-ic-shapes 0.04x, polymorphic-objects-v2 0.30x, sparse-array-v2 0.59x); the retained ten give 0.878x. 'Faster than Node on every row' is not met (21 of 30). The canonical raw JSON reports zipp 0.0.12 while the README says 0.0.13. The WASM build is slower than QuickJS-NG: v0.0.5 adjusted 2.107x, and v0.0.6 compared only 5 of 30 rows (0.96x). The five-kernel WASM speed-up (0.095x QuickJS-NG) was dominated by exact bytecode-shape lanes (1.815x with them off). Those lanes (vm/array_ops.rs) compile only when not (jit and x86_64), so the native x86-64 captures exclude them. The project is a rapid, largely machine-assisted rewrite with 6 stars; Rust, not C++.

notes: Confirmed and upgraded C to A on the QuickJS-NG interpreter comparison: public harness and corpus, Rust 1.92.0 flags, a hash-pinned official baseline binary, and a named CPU. The only gap is the unstamped MSYS2 GCC revision of the official QuickJS-NG build; cap at C if that counts as a missing compiler. Shortcomings to record: the Node/Bun/Deno numbers come from pre-B280 code that had a later-fixed call-order correctness bug (C-grade on their own) and regressed afterwards; the QuickJS-NG raw JSONs are not committed; the results are historical (v0.0.5 and v0.0.6, six reps); the WASM build is slower than QuickJS-NG; and the WASM kernel claim depended on exact-shape lanes, which the native build excludes.
